EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  
“Import Competition, Technology Adoption, and Reallocation in Europe, 1996-2007”

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Primary strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study extension, combined with an instrumental-variables (IV) “shift–share” approach.

Why DID?  
• The removal of long-standing textile & clothing quotas after China’s WTO entry created a discrete, plausibly exogenous surge in Chinese import penetration that differed sharply across narrowly defined products according to pre-2001 quota coverage.  
• We observe firms before and after the shock, allowing us to compare outcomes in “high-quota” (treated) versus “low-quota” (control) industries.

Why IV?  
• Import penetration may still react endogenously to EU demand. We therefore instrument country-industry-year Chinese import penetration with (i) the interaction of pre-2001 quota coverage and post-2001 years, and (ii) a standard Bartik variable: growth of Chinese exports to the United States in the same product, interacted with each EU country’s pre-1996 industry mix.

The DID gives transparent event-study pictures and the IV addresses remaining endogeneity.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Continuous: ΔChinaPen_icty = (China imports_ict / (domestic production + total imports – exports)_ict).  
The endogenous regressor in the firm equation is ΔChinaPen_icty measured at the country-industry (i, c) and year t level.

Instrument 1 (Quota‐based):  
Quota_ic × Post_t , where  
• Quota_ic = share of 1996-2000 imports in product p that was quota-constrained (0–1) averaged over 1996-2000, aggregated to 4-digit SIC i for country c.  
• Post_t = 1 for 2002–2007, 0 for 1996–2001.

Instrument 2 (Bartik):  
Bartik_icty = Σ_p s_icp,1996 × ΔUSChinaImport_pt ,  
where s_icp,1996 is country-industry-product p’s share of imports in 1996.

Control group  
Firms in industries with Quota_ic ≈ 0 (bottom quartile) provide the counterfactual trend.

Treatment timing  
Event date: 2002 (partial removal); robustness checks treat 2005 (full removal) as a second shock. Event-study horizons: t = –5,…,+6 relative to 2001.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: Absent quota removal, outcomes in high- and low-quota industries would have evolved similarly.  
Plausible because quota coverage was negotiated in the 1950s-1970s, long before modern European competitive conditions.

A2. Quota coverage predetermined: Pre-2001 quota intensity is orthogonal to differential technology trends in the 1990s.  
Plausible; the original MFA bargaining reflected political economy of the 1960s/70s, not impending IT or patent booms.

A3. No general-equilibrium spillovers that differentially hit control industries at the same time.  
Partly plausible; we mitigate by including country×year and industry×year fixed effects.

A4. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): Firms do not simultaneously compete in many 4-digit industries.  
Reasonably plausible given four-digit assignment but we check multi-product firms separately.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential pre-trends → event-study graphs; inclusion of industry-specific linear trends; placebo tests using 1996-2001 only.

T2. Demand shocks correlated with China penetration (e.g., IKEA-led furniture boom).  
→ IV strategy with quota and US-based Bartik predictor; include country×industry fixed effects to net out persistent demand levels.

T3. Measurement error in Chinese import shares due to misclassification across 6-digit products.  
→ Aggregate instruments over broader HS2 clusters as robustness; cluster standard errors at country-industry level.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages ----------------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)     # fast felm-type regressions
library(haven)      # if Stata dta files appear
library(ivreg)      # 2SLS
library(modelsummary)
# 1. Load Data ---------------------------------------------------------
firm   <- read_csv("firms_panel_1996_2007.csv")      # Amadeus + patents + IT
trade  <- read_csv("china_imports_hs6_1996_2007.csv")# UN Comtrade
prod   <- read_csv("eurostat_prodcom.csv")           # domestic prod
quota  <- read_csv("mfa_quota_shares.csv")           # product-level quota %
us_trd <- read_csv("us_china_imports_hs6.csv")       # for Bartik

# 2. Construct Industry-Year China Penetration ------------------------
trade_eu <- trade %>% 
  mutate(china_share = china_import_value) %>%            # rename
  left_join(prod, by = c("country","industry","year")) %>% 
  mutate(demand = domestic_production + total_imports - exports,
         china_pen = china_share / demand)

# 3. Build Instruments -------------------------------------------------
# (i) Quota-based interaction
quota_ind <- quota %>% 
  group_by(country, industry) %>% 
  summarise(quota_pre = mean(quota_share[year %in% 1996:2000], na.rm=T))

china_pen_iv <- trade_eu %>% 
  left_join(quota_ind, by = c("country","industry")) %>% 
  mutate(post  = ifelse(year >= 2002, 1, 0),
         quota_iv = quota_pre * post)

# (ii) Bartik instrument
us_growth <- us_trd %>% 
  group_by(product, year) %>% 
  summarise(us_cn_imp = sum(value)) %>% 
  arrange(product, year) %>% 
  group_by(product) %>% 
  mutate(g_us = log(us_cn_imp) - log(lag(us_cn_imp)))

weights <- trade %>% 
  filter(year == 1996) %>% 
  mutate(weight = import_value / sum(import_value)) %>% 
  select(country, industry, product, weight)

bartik_iv <- weights %>% 
  left_join(us_growth, by = c("product")) %>% 
  group_by(country, industry, year) %>% 
  summarise(bartik = sum(weight * g_us, na.rm=TRUE))

china_pen_iv <- china_pen_iv %>% left_join(bartik_iv, 
                        by = c("country","industry","year"))

# 4. Merge with firm panel --------------------------------------------
firm_full <- firm %>% 
  left_join(china_pen_iv, by = c("country","industry","year")) 

# 5. Main 2SLS Regression (patents as outcome) -------------------------
# y_fict = β * ChinaPen_icty + γX + FE
reg_2sls <- feols(log1p(patent_apps) ~  china_pen | 
                   quota_iv + bartik ~ 
                   firm_id + industry#year + country#year, 
                   data = firm_full, 
                   cluster = ~country^industry)

etable(reg_2sls, se = "cluster")

# 6. Event Study (visual pre-trends) ----------------------------------
firm_full <- firm_full %>% 
  mutate(rel_year = year - 2001,
         treat    = (quota_pre > quantile(quota_pre, .75)))

event_est <- feols(TFP ~ i(rel_year, treat, ref = -1) + 
                   firm_id + industry#year + country#year, 
                   data = firm_full, cluster = ~industry^country)

iplot(event_est)  # visual check

# 7. Robustness: Drop textile/apparel-heavy countries ------------------
robust <- feols(log1p(patent_apps) ~ china_pen | quota_iv + bartik ~ 
                firm_id + industry#year + country#year,
                data = filter(firm_full, !country %in% c("Italy","Spain")),
                cluster = ~country^industry)
etable(reg_2sls, robust, se="cluster")
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Theory predicts “X-efficiency” effects: surviving firms facing tougher import competition innovate and adopt IT faster, while marginal low-tech firms exit.  
• Patent applications: +5-10 % for a one s.d. rise in ChinaPen.  
• IT intensity: +3 computers per 100 workers (≈½ s.d.).  
• TFP: +2 p.p. within survivors.  
Aggregate employment: –3 % in high-quota industries owing to exit and offshoring.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID/IV)
C1. No differential pre-trends (parallel trends) ............. 1  
C2. Exogenous treatment assignment (quota predetermined) ...... 1  
C3. No anticipation or spillover effects ..................... 0.5 (some off-setting GE effects possible)  
C4. Instrument relevance & strength .......................... 1 (quota_iv F-stat > 10 expected)  
C5. Correct inference (clustering, multiple testing) ......... 1  

Total ≈ 4.5 / 5 → Good but still monitor spillovers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
This plan couples transparent DID graphs with a strong historical instrument to deliver credible causal estimates of how Chinese import competition accelerated technical change and reshaped European manufacturing.
